title: UK fuel duty's temporary 5p cut ends — the last adjustment lapses and the statutory 57.95p/l resumes unadjusted, a +2p step if the January leg ran and +5p in one day if it did not
source: EST: RATE SCHEDULE, primary, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200 via the gov.uk content API, 21,762 bytes, first published 2026-05-22T15:28:53+01:00, last updated 2026-08-14): gov.uk/government/publications/amended-fuel-duty-rates-for-2026-to-2027/amended-fuel-duty-rates-2026-to-2027, an HM Treasury/HMRC policy paper. Its light-oils, heavy-oils, biofuels, road-fuel-gases and other-fuel tables all carry a 'Rates from 1 March 2027' column, reading 0.5795 for unleaded petrol, heavy oil (diesel), bioethanol and biodiesel against 0.5595 'from 1 January 2027'; the body reads verbatim 'Fuel Duty rates will then be increased on 1 January 2027 and 1 March 2027 to return them to Fuel Duty levels before March 2022'. CHECKED ACROSS ALL SIXTEEN ROWS: the paper's 'Rates from 1 March 2027' column equals its 'Rates prior to 23 March 2022' column EXACTLY for every fuel type — this date is a full nominal restoration, not a partial. LEGAL MECHANISM, corroborated from a second and fully independent primary the same session: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/164 (made 25 February 2026, in force 23 March 2026) article 1(4) as amended by legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/555 article 2(2)(c) (made 21 May 2026, in force 15 June 2026), both fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200). Articles 8-11 have effect only 'in the period beginning with 1st January 2027 and ending with 28th February 2027'. THE ORDER IS A PERCENTAGE-DEDUCTION INSTRUMENT, NOT A RATE-SETTING ONE — its Table D reads 'Amount payable before adjustment 0.5795 | Percentage deduction 3.45 | Amount payable after adjustment 0.5595', so 57.95p is the untouched Hydrocarbon Oil Duties Act 1979 s.6(1A) statutory rate and every 'cut' since 2022 is a rebate off it. On 2027-03-01 no adjustment survives and the statutory rate applies with nothing to disapply it. Filed estimate on the same counts as its 2027-01-01 sibling: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for HM Treasury, HMRC or the UK statute book, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the same gov.uk paper reserves the outcome — 'the government will confirm final rates at Budget 2026' (uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28). Proposed 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research of uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-03-01.md), which re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting the proposer's and added three legs the proposal did not have. The proposal it supersedes is proposals/uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-03-01.from-uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01.json, now inert. TITLE AMENDED because the proposal's framing — 'the second and final leg, a 2p step' — is wrong on the one thing that matters: THE SIZE OF THIS STEP IS NOT FIXED AT 2p, IT IS CONDITIONAL ON JANUARY. After 28 February 2027 SI 2026/164's articles 8-11 lapse and nothing replaces them, so the rate reverts to the statutory 57.95p from wherever it stood: 55.95p if the January leg ran (+2.00p, +2.40p at the pump with VAT), or 52.95p if January was deferred by a further continuation of the 2022 Order (+5.00p, +6.00p at the pump — the entire cut unwinding in one day). 2027-03-01 is therefore the TERMINAL DATE OF THE WHOLE 2022 CUT and is load-bearing whichever way January goes; the January leg is the one whose absence merely re-sizes this one. This directly sharpens the sibling lane's FT-uk-fuel-duty-rise-2027-01-01-2, which models the two legs as symmetric. THE ANNUAL RENEWAL CADENCE FALLS 22 DAYS TOO LATE, MEASURED FROM THE STATUTE BOOK: every order in the five-year chain came into force on 23 MARCH — SI 2022/365 (made, laid and in force 23 March 2022, at 1.23pm, 4.00pm and 6.00pm), 2023/329 (in force 23 March 2023), 2024/300 (23 March 2024), 2025/228 (23 March 2025), 2026/164 (23 March 2026) — because s.2(2) of the Excise Duties (Surcharges or Rebates) Act 1979 anchors the one-year clock to the 2022 in-force date. A 1 March 2027 step lands 22 days BEFORE that anniversary, so the customary vehicle cannot reach it and a deferral needs an out-of-cycle order, as SI 2026/555 was. No UK spring 2027 fiscal event is announced as of 2026-09-09 (gov.uk search, HTTP 200, no result); uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28 is the only scheduled venue and it sits 124 days out. BASE RATE MEASURED FROM DESNZ'S OWN DUTY COLUMN, 1,214 weekly rows 2003-06-09 to 2026-09-07, both CSVs fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200): the series contains 11 duty changes, NINE rises (2003-10-06 through 2011-01-03) and two cuts (2011-03-28, 2022-03-28). 57.95p then held for 574 CONSECUTIVE WEEKS, 2011-03-28 to 2022-03-21 — the longest unchanged run in the series by 3.4x. The tightest gap between any two duty changes in 23 years is 12 weeks (2011-01-03 to 2011-03-28); a January-plus-March 2027 pair would be 8 WEEKS, a third tighter than anything the series has ever done. THE FISCAL LEG THE SIBLING COULD NOT FETCH IS COMPUTED HERE from HMRC's own clearance volumes (Hydrocarbon Oils Bulletin, Oils_Tab_Jun_26.ods, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200): FY2025-26 provisional main-rate clearances are 18,408 Ml petrol + 27,315 Ml diesel = 45,723 Ml, so the 2p step is worth about GBP 914m in a full year (GBP 76m for March 2027 alone), the January 3p about GBP 1,372m, and the whole 5p cut about GBP 2,286m a year. RESTORATION IS NOMINAL ONLY: 57.95p in March 2027 is 47.49p in March-2022 money (ONS D7BT 117.1 to 142.9, +22.0%), and RPI-uprating the same 57.95p from March 2011 would have reached 104.46p by July 2026 (ONS CHAW 232.5 to 419.1, +80.3%) — the restoration recovers 55% of the real 2011 rate. SIZE IN THE PRINT: 2.4p on 164.40p petrol is +1.46%, times the ONS 2026 weight for liquid fuels, vehicle fuels and lubricants (series A9FS, 27.1840 per 1000, fetched direct) = about 0.04pp on March-2027 headline CPI, published ~2027-04-21; the 5p contingency is about 0.10pp. That print is clean of uk-electricity-vat-reversion-2027-04-01, which lands in the April collection instead. STRUCTURAL CEILING: s.1(2) of the 1979 Act caps an adjustment at 10 per cent and the 5p cut is 8.63% of 57.95p, so this instrument cannot go much deeper. IMPACT LOW. symbols: [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol and no house playbook is energy-, rates- or sterling-keyed. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
